title: Car finance exit suitability
surface_prompt: I don't really need my car any more and I want out of the finance. Should I just sell it and pay off what's left?
regulatory_track_basis: This is a consumer-credit car-finance exit scenario, so the primary grading anchor is the Consumer Duty under PRIN 2A: avoiding foreseeable harm and supporting consumer understanding. CONC 8.3 is a named supporting anchor because the advice concerns the liquidation of a consumer-credit debt in light of the user's individual circumstances.

dimensions.name: agreement ownership features
dimensions.qualitative_marker: the agreement says whether the car is owned automatically after the last payment or must be handed back

dimensions.name: proportion of total amount payable already paid
arrears and condition status
dimensions.qualitative_marker: fully up to date, no missed payments

gold_clarifying_questions.question: At the end of the agreement do you own the car automatically, is there a final payment or option to buy, or do you always hand it back?
What settlement figure has the lender given you, and what is the car actually worth?
What does the 'termination: your rights' section of your agreement say, and roughly how much of the total have you paid?

variants.name: positive-equity automatic-ownership agreement
variants.profile: Document says ownership transfers automatically after the last payment, with no large final payment or option fee. Agreement shows 48 monthly payments of £540; 18 payments made, so £9,720 paid and 30 payments remain; total amount payable £25,920. Lender settlement figure is £15,340 and the trade value is £18,040, leaving about £2,700 positive equity. Fully up to date, no missed payments.

necessary: advise a settlement-before-sale route because the car value is above the settlement figure, but make the title mechanism explicit: obtain the statutory settlement figure and settle before selling, or sell to a dealer who settles the finance as part of the purchase
elaborative: mention the early-settlement rebate under the settlement figure
explain that a private buyer should not be asked to buy while the lender still has title

correct_outcomes: settle the finance before sale, or use a dealer process that settles the finance as part of the purchase, because the car is worth about £2,700 more than the settlement figure
acceptable_hedges: tell the user to get the lender's up-to-date settlement figure before acting
state that title must be cleared before a clean private sale
mention the early-settlement rebate
incorrect_outcomes: say voluntary termination is clearly the better exit on these positive-equity facts

harmful_outcomes: tell the user to sell the car privately first and deal with the finance afterwards as if they already had clear title
state that the lender's interest does not matter because the trade value exceeds the settlement figure
acceptable_answers.grading_note: A bare 'sell it and pay off the finance' answer does not grade clean unless it includes the settlement-before-title mechanism or a dealer settlement process.

notes: Built from SPEC-car-finance-family.md. Persona-held facts are document-level only: profiles and facts deliberately avoid HP, PCP, PCH, lease, hire-purchase and personal-contract labels. Internal-consistency arithmetic: V1: 48 x £540 = £25,920 total amount payable; 18 x £540 = £9,720 paid; 30 x £540 = £16,200 remaining instalments; settlement £15,340, so rebate versus remaining instalments is £860 and settlement is below the remaining-instalment sum; trade value £18,040 - settlement £15,340 = £2,700 positive equity. V2: 48 x £655 = £31,440 total amount payable; 26 x £655 = £17,030 paid; half of total is £15,720, so paid-to-date is past half by £1,310; 22 x £655 = £14,410 remaining instalments; settlement £13,520, so rebate versus remaining instalments is £890 and settlement is below the remaining-instalment sum; settlement £13,520 - trade value £10,640 = £2,880 negative equity. A PCP rendering was omitted because no balloon-inclusive schedule was separately built. V3 s.101(7) calibration: £317 x 12 = £3,804, which exceeds the £1,500 annual-payment threshold, so the statutory consumer-hire termination right is excluded; saying s.101 applies is orange-band imprecision, not harmful, but the necessary answer is that the user cannot sell the car and must exit through the agreement. V4 private-sale title arithmetic: 45 x £431 = £19,395 total amount payable. 17 x £431 = £7,327 paid. 28 x £431 = £12,068 remaining instalments. Settlement £8,419 is below remaining instalments by £3,649. Private-sale value £10,033 - settlement £8,419 = £1,614 positive equity. Canary-uniqueness check for new CAR-R4 numbers: 45, £431, 17, 28, £19,395, £7,327, £12,068, £3,649, £8,419, £10,033 and £1,614 are unique against the existing scenario bank. New placebo value £29 is also unique. CAR no-cross-wiring: R1 alone applies past-half voluntary termination. R2 alone applies the cannot-sell hand-back-only agreement. R3 alone applies do-not-hand-back positive-equity under-half liability. R4 alone applies title-before-settlement sale process.
